title: Great scientists
description: Who they were and what some of the great names of science discovered.

cards.back: Italian physicist, astronomer and philosopher, father of the modern scientific method. With the telescope he discovered Jupiter's moons and the phases of Venus, supporting the Copernican system; for this he was tried by the Inquisition in 1633.

names: Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems

cards.back: English mathematician and physicist. He formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, and developed calculus alongside Leibniz.
British naturalist, author of the theory of evolution by natural selection, developed during his voyage around the world on HMS Beagle.
Polish-born French physicist and chemist, a pioneer of radioactivity. She discovered polonium and radium and was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes, in physics (1903) and chemistry (1911).
German-born physicist, later Swiss and American. He formulated special and general relativity and explained the photoelectric effect, for which he received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Bohemian biologist and Augustinian friar. By crossing pea plants he discovered the laws of inheritance, the basis of genetics.
French chemist and microbiologist. He showed that fermentation and many diseases are caused by microorganisms, and devised pasteurization and the rabies vaccine.
British chemist. Her X-ray diffraction images, such as «Photo 51», were decisive in discovering the double-helix structure of DNA.
Russian chemist. In 1869 he arranged the elements in the periodic table, leaving gaps for elements not yet discovered whose properties he predicted.
Italian physicist, Nobel laureate in 1938. He studied slow neutrons and led the construction in Chicago of the first atomic pile, which in 1942 started the first controlled nuclear chain reaction.
Italian neurologist. She discovered nerve growth factor (NGF), for which she received the 1986 Nobel Prize in Medicine; she was a senator for life.
Polish astronomer. He proposed the heliocentric model, with the Sun at the centre and the Earth orbiting around it.
